Today, a short video found in the candidate version of macOS Tahoe 26.7 allegedly demonstrates the "Visual Intelligence" feature of Apple's long-rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Let's take a look together.

macOS 26.7 contains a demo video of camera-equipped AirPods

Yesterday, MacRumors discovered a short video in the candidate version of macOS Tahoe 26.7. In the video, a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to log the book he is currently reading, and Siri's voiceover says:

The video does not show the camera itself; the earbuds look very similar to the current AirPods Pro, with the most obvious difference being that the stems appear to be slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris also posted the same video on the X platform:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods later this year, with the internal codename B790. Earlier, MacRumors also found information related to B790 in the candidate version of macOS 26.7, including code referencing "image streaming".

Interestingly, this AirPods is a different product from another camera-equipped model with the internal codename B798, which is expected to launch in 2027.

Judging from Apple's choice to include this demo video in the candidate version of macOS 26.7, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to make their official debut at next month's iPhone event.

What do you think of this video? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
